description: Per-shikigami material-pattern definitions: which named material sections are shown for patterns P1-P5 while others are hidden.

ID.technical: FName row key referenced by ShikigamiDataTable.Id_ShikigamiMaterial. Both UGameShikigamiMaterialController::SetMaterialPattern (retail 0x141497b80) and the targeted-show variant resolve the row from ShikigamiMaterialDataTables (+0x6D0) using Shikigami_FindRow; None/missing rows leave materials unchanged. 3 exported rows.

MaterialName_P1.technical: TArray<FName> (7 slots in every exported row, NAME_None padded). Pattern index 0 selects this array; the controller builds 8 pattern entries, sorts the selected one first and calls ShowMaterialSections(mesh, indices, bShow) for each valid name, hiding the other patterns' sections. Export CN_040 P1: MI_CN_040_00_Outline.

MaterialName_P2.technical: TArray<FName> selected by Pattern==1; same show-this/hide-others path. Export CN_040 P2: MI_CN_040_00_Outline_P1 and MI_CN_040_00_Ring_P1.

MaterialName_P3.technical: TArray<FName> selected by Pattern==2; all three exported rows leave it entirely NAME_None, so choosing this pattern hides the other named sections without showing any new material in this data set.

MaterialName_P4.technical: TArray<FName> selected by Pattern==3; all three exported rows are entirely NAME_None.

MaterialName_P5.technical: TArray<FName> selected by Pattern==4; all three exported rows are entirely NAME_None. Patterns 5..7 are accepted by the retail bounds check (0..7) but have no corresponding arrays in this shikigami row struct (the character-material twin has P6..P8), so they only hide the named sections.

notes: ShikigamiMaterialDataTables is manager slot +0x6D0; registered at GameDataTableManager.cpp:411 and resolved at line 239.
The row names are material-section/parameter names looked up in the shikigami material controller's MaterialParameters cache (ShowMaterialSections, 0x12e65a0); they are not material asset paths.

The second consumer (GameShikigami.cpp:1787) is the slot-190 'set material pattern' interface path, which only shows the selected pattern's materials and stores MaterialPattern; the first consumer (1710) also hides all others.
Do not confuse this with CharacterMaterialDataTable or ShikigamiMaterialDataTable's character twin; the latter has eight P arrays while this struct has five.

usages.detail: UGameShikigamiMaterialController::SetMaterialPattern resolves the row from the shikigami's Id_ShikigamiMaterial and toggles section visibility for P1-P5 (retail 0x141497b80).
Interface slot 190 resolves the same row and shows the selected pattern's named materials without explicitly hiding others.
Documents the row linkage and pattern indices; the controller caches material parameters by these names.
